b55f530 feat: support Zig typed arrays and DataView
     1	# Go–Zig binary flat-codec interoperability
     2	
     3	The deliverable is a shared binary-value surface on which Go v5, Go v6 and Zig
     4	can exchange upstream devalue 5.9.4 flat documents. The user corrected the
     5	previous milestone: an independently working Zig codec is insufficient when
     6	the Go peer rejects its values. Both Go modules still pin 5.9.4; this change
     7	does not claim v6 parity with upstream 6.x.
     8	
     9	## Result
    10	
    11	Extend the existing Go `*TypedArray` and `*DataView` model, without changing
    12	exported field types, to `Stringify` and `Parse`. Support all twelve upstream
    13	typed-array tags, including Float16Array, plus DataView. Transport raw backing
    14	bytes, preserve view kind/extent, repeated view identity, distinct equal
    15	views, shared backing buffers and graph cycles. Use the upstream compact/full-
    16	extent wire spelling and buffer-slot allocation order. Reducer/reviver
    17	precedence remains intact.
    18	
    19	Add `NewArrayBuffer([]byte)` as a copying constructor with distinct allocation
    20	even for an empty buffer. Existing slice literals continue to work; a nil or
    21	zero-capacity empty slice cannot express distinct buffer ownership. Decode
    22	empty buffers into owned storage and key empty buffers with positive capacity
    23	by their backing allocation. Apply the identity rule to both serializers.
    24	Document the constructor requirement for empty shared buffers. Do not change
    25	the ArrayBuffer slice type or introduce a parallel view model.
    26	
    27	Both Stringify and Uneval use the same native view validation. It rejects
    28	unknown constructors, nil view pointers, negative/out-of-range extents and
    29	misaligned typed offsets/byte lengths. Bound arithmetic uses
    30	subtraction/division so it cannot overflow. Decoder validation checks the
    31	referenced raw slot is ArrayBuffer before hydration, then checks the revived
    32	value is an actual ArrayBuffer. Exercise self/mutual references and array-like
    33	allocation attacks with real reviver payloads, negative-sentinel and out-of-
    34	range backing-slot indices. Test invalid geometry in Uneval as well as
    35	Stringify. Reject geometry JavaScript cannot construct. For valid views
    36	preserve 5.9.4 expression bytes, including its partial-element quirk: a
    37	hoisted odd-sized buffer emits new T(buffer).subarray(...) that fails when
    38	evaluated; an inline one errors while rendering its whole element list. Record
    39	that pair as an upstream expectation; the corrected constructor spelling
    40	belongs to upstream 6.x (change-map row 14), not this parity target.
    41	
    42	Canonical upstream-produced view documents are the common decoding contract.
    43	Go keeps upstream's constructor semantics for optional offset/count fields
    44	where its existing model can express them; Zig already documents stricter
    45	integer/arity admission for manually crafted documents. Do not silently claim
    46	their malformed-input acceptance or every JavaScript coercion is identical.
    47	Float16 adds raw storage transport and requires correct Uneval rendering in
    48	both modules: half-to-double conversion, JS formatting including negative
    49	zero, and two-byte subarray geometry. An unhandled numeric kind must return an
    50	error rather than silently emit empty elements.
    51	
    52	## Validation
    53	
    54	Port the existing complete binary fixture inputs to native Go constructions in
    55	both modules. Expectations come from the pinned JavaScript recorder, never
    56	either port. The recorded corpus covers every kind, whole/sub/empty/odd-sized
    57	buffers, aliases, cycles, floating bit patterns, BigInt storage, copied Node
    58	Buffer sources, file bytes and reducers. Independently check decoded contents
    59	and identity; a successful same-codec round trip alone is insufficient. Add
    60	targeted malformed-wire and native-geometry tests, including upstream's raw-
    61	buffer guard and reviver precedence. Keep module tests self-contained and
    62	Node-free by recording their static fixtures under each testdata/. Each
    63	module's recorder uses its own pin, regenerates its own binary corpus and
    64	records targeted Float16 and empty-shared-buffer Uneval expectations. Native
    65	tests require every fixture version to match UpstreamVersion. Update the v6
    66	change map's stale binary assumptions and malformed-view parsing work item.
    67	
    68	Add a small root `test-interop` command to normal `just test`: native Go tests
    69	emit independently constructed upstream-verified documents for each module;
    70	native Zig tests decode those documents and compare against independently
    71	constructed graphs, then emit their own documents; Go tests decode the Zig
    72	documents and check their independently constructed expected values. Exchange
    73	temporary files only. Assert nonempty complete case counts and names in all
    74	phases, and fail on missing files when the integration recipe is invoked. Add
    75	a CI job with Go and mise-pinned Zig that runs this recipe. This is a direct
    76	codec integration check, not a new proof framework or generated tracking
    77	system. Native language suites continue to run without starting Node or the
    78	other language compiler.
    79	
    80	Run `just test`, `just lint`, Zig ReleaseSafe tests and relevant Go consumer
    81	tests only after redirecting their legacy polytype/devalue imports in scratch
    82	consumer copies to this runtime; go.work alone is vacuous because both
    83	consumers still import polytype's bundled codec. Report this redirection and
    84	any unavailable consumer proof explicitly. Production consumer migration
    85	remains a separate task (ephemeral/polytype-migration.md); until it happens
    86	that bundled runtime still cannot exchange binary views with Zig. Audit and
    87	name remaining cross-language differences (including sparse-array allocation
    88	limits and native identity limitations); do not label binary interoperability
    89	as complete upstream feature parity. Retain upstream behavior coverage from
    90	the previous milestone and update stale capability descriptions.
    91	
    92	## Review and delivery
    93	
    94	Claude Opus reviews this plan through the consensus skill before
    95	implementation, and reviews the completed change and proof again before a PR.
    96	Resolve material findings with ordinary tests and source evidence; the user
    97	expressly rejects elaborate proof machinery. After consensus and passing
    98	checks, create and squash-merge the PR, synchronize main, and clean up task
    99	processes/worktree where the desktop app permits it.

# Adversarial review: Go–Zig binary flat-codec interoperability plan (round 04)

## Target

The revised `ephemeral/go-zig-flat-parity-plan.md` (untracked, on branch
`codex/go-zig-flat-parity` at `b55f530`) and
`ephemeral/worklog/20261008-go-zig-flat-parity.md`. Earlier rounds:
`ephemeral/reviews/20261008-go-zig-plan-round-0{1,2,3}.md`.

Caller constraints honoured: read-only apart from this artifact. The launch
prompt did not narrow the review's scope; this is a full re-review of the plan.

## Evidence inspected

- Repository instructions: `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` (parity promise, major and
  minor rules, consumers, working rules, worklog protocol), `justfile`,
  `mise.toml`, `.github/workflows/{go,zig}.yml`.
- Go v5 surroundings (v6 is a copy), re-checked against the plan's current
  text: `uneval_value.go`, `typedarray.go`, `uneval.go`, `stringify.go`,
  `internal.go`, `parse.go`.
- Upstream devalue 5.9.4 (pinned `v5/node_modules/devalue`): `stringify.js`
  view and buffer cases, `parse.js` view guard, `operations.js`
  `viewInfo`/`fromViewInfo`, `uneval.js` typed-array, DataView and Float16
  rendering. Upstream tests in `ephemeral/upstream-5.9.4/`.
- Recorders and the Zig version checks, `ephemeral/devalue-parity/5.9.2-to-6.0.2.md`,
  `ephemeral/polytype-migration.md`, and the consumer imports.
- Executions from earlier rounds that still hold for the current text: the
  scratch Float16 Uneval reproduction, the Uneval geometry reproduction, and
  the pinned-upstream and Go comparison for an odd-sized shared buffer.

## Status of earlier findings

| Round | Finding | Plan now | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01-1 | Float16 Uneval optional, and silently corrupt | Lines 47-50 | Resolved |
| 01-2 | Uneval changes lacked upstream evidence | Lines 63-64, 39 | Resolved |
| 01-3 | Interop not enforced in CI; gated tests skip silently | Lines 73-75 | Resolved |
| 01-4 | go.work consumer proof vacuous | Lines 80-86 | Resolved |
| 01-5 | v6 fixtures detached from pin; change map stale | Lines 62-66 | Resolved |
| 02-1 | Uneval skips geometry validation | Lines 27-29, 34-35 | Resolved |
| 02-2 | Sentinel and out-of-range buffer indices | Lines 32-34 | Resolved |
| 02-3 / 03-2 | Formatting | Rewrapped throughout | Resolved |
| 03-1 | "No failing constructor" contradicted 5.9.4 parity | Lines 35-40 | Resolved |

On 03-1, the plan now rejects only "geometry JavaScript cannot construct". For
valid views it keeps 5.9.4's exact Uneval behaviour, including the
partial-element quirk: a hoisted odd-sized buffer emits a failing
`new T(a).subarray(…)`, and an inline one returns an error. It records that
pair as an upstream expectation and assigns the corrected spelling to 6.x
(change-map row 14). This matches the pinned package's output and current Go
v5, as executed in round 03.

## Findings

No findings. I re-checked the following and found nothing material:

- **Parity promise.**
  - Wire spelling: compact when `byteLength !== bufferByteLength`, using the
    element count for typed arrays and the byte length for DataView.
  - Slot order: the view slot is allocated before its buffer.
  - Reducers run on the view's buffer, as upstream's `flatten(info.buffer)` does.
  - The raw-slot guard comes before hydration and the native buffer check after
    revival.
  - Float16 rendering, including `-0`, NaN and Infinity via `formatNumber`.
  - All of these follow `stringify.js:303-344`, `parse.js:174-197`,
    `operations.js` and `uneval.js:338-365, 634-652`.
- **API rules.**
  - Additions only: the `Float16Array` constant, `NewArrayBuffer`, and
    `BytesPerElement` returning 2 for a kind it previously rejected.
  - No exported field or type changes, so this fits a minor release within
    `/v5` and `/v6`.
  - The change lands in both maintained modules, as `AGENTS.md` requires.
- **Identity.** Keying empty buffers with positive capacity by allocation
  pointer is sound. A slice with positive capacity points inside its
  allocation, and zero-capacity reslices remain unkeyed. The plan documents the
  limitation for nil or zero-capacity slices and requires `NewArrayBuffer` for
  empty shared buffers. The Uneval hoisting change has recorded upstream
  expectations.
- **Evidence rules.**
  - Goldens come from each module's own pinned recorder, never from either
    port, and every fixture's version is checked.
  - Tests stay Node-free plain `go test`/`zig build test`.
  - `test-interop` exchanges temporary files only and generates no ledger.
  - It fails rather than skips when invoked, and CI runs it.
- **Scope.** Nothing is over-engineered. The interop recipe answers the user's
  recorded correction. Consumer proof is redirected or reported as unavailable,
  and production migration stays a separate plan. Cross-language and identity
  limitations must be named, without claiming full feature parity.

## Outcome

no findings

Review written to ephemeral/reviews/20261008-go-zig-plan-round-04.md. Outcome: no findings.

Every earlier finding is resolved in the current plan:
- Float16 Uneval rendering is required in both modules.
- Uneval expectations are recorded from the pinned upstream.
- The Go↔Zig exchange runs in CI and fails rather than skipping when invoked.
- Consumer tests run against redirected scratch copies, or the proof is reported as unavailable.
- Each module records its own fixtures from its own pin.
- Uneval geometry validation rejects only geometry JavaScript cannot construct.
- 5.9.4's odd-sized-buffer Uneval quirk is preserved, with the corrected spelling left to 6.x (change-map row 14).
- Formatting is fixed.

I also re-checked the rest of the plan and found no problems: wire format, slot order and reviver guards match upstream; the API changes are additive and go into both modules; empty-buffer identity is sound; the test rules hold; and nothing is over-engineered.

Only the review file was written; nothing outside ephemeral/ changed.
